sentences.zh: 高句麗 百濟 勿吉 失韋 豆莫婁 地豆于 庫莫奚 契丹 烏洛侯

translations.literal: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Wuluohou
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Wuluohou

sentences.zh: 高句麗者，出於夫餘，自言先祖朱蒙。

translations.literal: As for Goguryeo, it issued from Buyeo; they themselves say their founding ancestor was Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo arose from Buyeo; its people claim Jumong as their founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母河伯女，為夫餘王閉於室中，為日所照，引身避之，日影又逐。

translations.literal: Jumong's mother was a daughter of the River Lord. The king of Buyeo shut her in a room; she was struck by sunlight, drew back her body to avoid it, and the sun's shadow pursued her again.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother was a daughter of the River Lord. The king of Buyeo had her shut in a chamber; when sunlight fell upon her, she shrank away to avoid it, yet the sun's shadow followed her still.

sentences.zh: 既而有孕，生一卵，大如五升。

translations.literal: Thereafter she became pregnant and bore an egg as large as five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: She soon conceived and laid an egg the size of a five-sheng measure.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王棄之與犬，犬不食；

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo cast it to the dogs, but the dogs would not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo threw it to the dogs, but they would not touch it.

sentences.zh: 棄之與豕，豕又不食；

translations.literal: He cast it to the pigs, but the pigs likewise would not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: He gave it to the pigs, and they too refused to eat it.

sentences.zh: 棄之於路，牛馬避之；

translations.literal: He cast it on the road, and oxen and horses shunned it.
translations.idiomatic: He left it on the road, and cattle and horses turned aside from it.

sentences.zh: 後棄之野，眾鳥以毛茹之。

translations.literal: Later he cast it in the wild, and many birds warmed it with their feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he abandoned it in the open country, where flocks of birds covered it with their down to warm it.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王割剖之，不能破，遂還其母。

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo cut it open but could not break it, and so returned it to its mother.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo tried to cut the egg open but could not break the shell, and so gave it back to the mother.

sentences.zh: 其母以物裹之，置於暖處，有一男破殼而出。

translations.literal: His mother wrapped it in cloth and placed it in a warm spot; a boy broke the shell and came forth.
translations.idiomatic: She wrapped the egg in cloth and set it in a warm place, until a boy broke through the shell and was born.

sentences.zh: 及其長也，字之曰朱蒙，其俗言「朱蒙」者，善射也。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, they gave him the style-name Jumong; in their custom the word 'Jumong' means skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up they styled him Jumong, which in their tongue means 'skilled archer.'

sentences.zh: 夫餘人以朱蒙非人所生，將有異志，請除之，王不聽，命之養馬。

translations.literal: The people of Buyeo, holding that Jumong was not born of a human and would harbor rebellious intent, asked that he be put to death; the king would not listen and ordered him to raise horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Buyeo people, believing Jumong was not human-born and would prove disloyal, urged the king to kill him; the king refused and set him to tend the royal horses.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙每私試，知有善惡，駿者減食令瘦，駑者善養令肥。

translations.literal: Jumong would secretly test the horses in private, discerning which were good and which bad; for the swift he reduced feed to make them lean, and for the slow he fed them well to make them fat.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong secretly tested each horse to learn its quality: he cut the rations of the swift ones until they grew lean, and he fed the slow ones generously until they grew fat.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王以肥者自乘，以瘦者給朱蒙。

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo rode the fat ones himself and gave the lean ones to Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo kept the fat horses for himself and gave Jumong only the lean ones.

sentences.zh: 後狩于田，以朱蒙善射，限之一矢。

translations.literal: Later, on a hunt in the fields, because Jumong was skilled in archery they limited him to one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a hunt, they allowed Jumong only a single arrow because of his renown as an archer.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙雖矢少，殪獸甚多。

translations.literal: Though Jumong had few arrows, he slew very many beasts.
translations.idiomatic: With that one arrow Jumong nevertheless brought down a great number of game.

sentences.zh: 夫餘之臣又謀殺之。

translations.literal: The ministers of Buyeo again plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of Buyeo again conspired to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母陰知，告朱蒙曰：「國將害汝，以汝才略，宜遠適四方。

translations.literal: Jumong's mother learned of it in secret and told Jumong, saying, 'The state is about to harm you; given your talent and resourcefulness, you ought to flee far away to the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother learned of the plot in secret and warned him: 'The realm means to destroy you. With your gifts, you should flee far beyond its borders.'

sentences.zh: 」朱蒙乃與烏引、烏違等二人，棄夫餘，東南走。

translations.literal: Jumong then, together with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two others, abandoned Buyeo and fled southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong then left Buyeo with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two companions and fled toward the southeast.

sentences.zh: 中道遇一大水，欲濟無梁，夫餘人追之甚急。

translations.literal: Midway they came upon a great river; they wished to cross but there was no bridge, and the men of Buyeo pressed the pursuit closely.
translations.idiomatic: On the way they reached a great river with no bridge to cross it, while the Buyeo pursuers closed in fast behind them.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙告水曰：「我是日子，河伯外孫，今日逃走，追兵垂及，如何得濟？

translations.literal: Jumong addressed the water, saying, 'I am a child of the sun, the River Lord's grandson. Today I flee, and the pursuers are almost upon me—how am I to cross?'
translations.idiomatic: Jumong called to the river: 'I am a son of the sun, grandson of the River Lord. I flee for my life and the pursuers are almost upon me—how can I cross?'

sentences.zh: 」於是魚鼈並浮，為之成橋，朱蒙得渡，魚鼈乃解，追騎不得渡。

translations.literal: Thereupon fish and turtles all floated up and formed a bridge for him; Jumong crossed, the fish and turtles then dispersed, and the pursuing horsemen could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: At once fish and turtles rose to the surface and formed a bridge. Jumong crossed safely; when the creatures dispersed, the pursuers could not follow.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙遂至普述水，遇見三人，其一人著麻衣，一人著納衣，一人著水藻衣，與朱蒙至紇升骨城，遂居焉，號曰高句麗，因以為氏焉。

translations.literal: Jumong then reached the Pusu River, where he met three men—one wearing hemp cloth, one wearing coarse cloth, and one wearing waterweed cloth—who went with Jumong to Kesunggol City, where they settled; they were styled Goguryeo, and this became their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong came to the Pusu River and met three men, one in hemp, one in coarse cloth, and one in garments of waterweed. Together they went to Kesunggol City and made it their seat. They took the name Goguryeo, which became their royal clan.

sentences.zh: 初，朱蒙在夫餘時，妻懷孕，朱蒙逃後生一子，字始閭諧。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Jumong was still in Buyeo, his wife was pregnant; after Jumong fled she bore a son, styled Shilüxie.
translations.idiomatic: While Jumong was still in Buyeo his wife had been pregnant; after he fled she gave birth to a son styled Shilüxie.

sentences.zh: 及長，知朱蒙為國主，即與母亡而歸之，名之曰閭達，委之國事。

translations.literal: When he had grown up and learned that Jumong was ruler of the state, he fled with his mother to join him; Jumong named him Lüda and entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy grew up and learned that Jumong had become king, he fled with his mother to join him. Jumong named him Lüda and placed the affairs of state in his hands.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙死，閭達代立。

translations.literal: When Jumong died, Lüda succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jumong's death, Lüda succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 閭達死，子如栗代立。

translations.literal: When Lüda died, his son Yuli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lüda died, his son Yuli took the throne.

sentences.zh: 如栗死，子莫來代立，乃征夫餘，夫餘大敗，遂統屬焉。

translations.literal: When Yuli died, his son Molai succeeded; he then campaigned against Buyeo, Buyeo suffered a great defeat, and he brought it under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuli died, his son Molai became king, marched against Buyeo, routed it utterly, and brought the kingdom under Goguryeo's dominion.

sentences.zh: 莫來子孫相傳，至裔孫宮，生而開目能視，國人惡之。

translations.literal: Molai's descendants succeeded one another down to a distant descendant, Gong, who was born with his eyes open and able to see; the people of the state detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Molai's line passed from heir to heir until a distant descendant, Gong, was born with his eyes already open. The people regarded this as an evil omen.

sentences.zh: 及長凶虐，國以殘破。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was cruel and tyrannical, and the state was reduced to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew to manhood he proved cruel and tyrannical, and the kingdom fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 宮曾孫位宮亦生而視，人以其似曾祖宮，故名為位宮，高句麗呼相似為「位」。

translations.literal: Gong's great-great-grandson Weigong was also born able to see; because he resembled his great-great-grandfather Gong, he was named Weigong—in Goguryeo speech 'wei' means 'resemblance.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong's great-great-grandson Weigong was likewise born with his eyes open. Because he resembled his ancestor Gong, he was named Weigong—the Goguryeo word wei meaning 'likeness.'

sentences.zh: 位宮亦有勇力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Weigong likewise had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong too was brave and strong and excelled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中，入寇遼西安平，[1]為幽州刺史毋丘儉所破。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei he raided Anping in Liaoxi and was defeated by Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei reign-period Zhengshi he invaded Anping in western Liaodong and was defeated by Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其玄孫乙弗利，利子釗，烈帝時與慕容氏相攻擊。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandson Yifuli had a son Li and a grandson Chao; in the time of Emperor Lie they fought back and forth with the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant in the fifth generation was Yifuli; Li was Yifuli's son and Chao was Li's son. In the reign of Emperor Lie, Chao waged war against the Murong.

sentences.zh: 建國四年，慕容元真率眾伐之，入自南陝，戰於木底，大破釗軍，乘勝長驅，遂入丸都，釗單馬奔竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jian'guo, Murong Yuanzhen led his host against him, entered by way of Nanshan, fought at Mudi, routed Chao's army, pressed the victory in a long pursuit, entered Wandu, and Chao fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jian'guo, Murong Yuanzhen marched against him by the southern pass, defeated Chao's army at Mudi, drove deep into Goguryeo territory, and took Wandu while Chao fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 元真掘釗父墓，載其屍，并掠其母妻、珍寶、男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都城而還。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen dug up the tomb of Chao's father and carried off the corpse; he also seized Chao's mother and wife, treasures, and more than fifty thousand men and women, burned the palaces, destroyed the walls of Wandu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen opened the tomb of Chao's father and carried off the corpse, together with Chao's mother and wife, the royal treasures, and more than fifty thousand captives. He burned the palaces, razed the walls of Wandu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自後釗遣使來朝，阻隔寇讎，不能自達。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chao sent envoys to court, but they were blocked by enemies and could not reach their destination.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Chao sent tribute missions to the court, but enemies along the route barred the way and none could arrive.

sentences.zh: 釗後為百濟所殺。

translations.literal: Later Chao was killed by Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was later killed by Baekje.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，釗曾孫璉始遣使者安東奉表貢方物，并請國諱。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, Chao's great-great-grandson Lian first sent the envoy Andong to present a memorial and tribute goods, and also requested the imperial taboo names.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Chao's descendant Lian in the fifth generation first sent the envoy Andong with a memorial, local products as tribute, and a request for the imperial taboo names.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其誠款，詔下帝系名諱於其國，遣員外散騎侍郎李敖拜璉為都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu commended his sincerity, ordered the imperial genealogy and taboo names sent to his state, and dispatched Li Ao, Attendant Cavalier Outside the Regular Establishment, to invest Lian as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Concurrent Protector of the Eastern Yi as Central Commandant, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu praised his sincerity, sent down the imperial genealogy and taboo names to his kingdom, and dispatched Li Ao to invest Lian as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 敖至其所居平壤城，訪其方事，云：遼東南一千餘里，東至柵城，南至小海，北至舊夫餘，民戶參倍於前。

translations.literal: When Ao reached his seat at Pyongyang City and inquired into local affairs, it was reported: south of Liaodong more than a thousand li, east to Seong Fortress, south to the Lesser Sea, north to old Buyeo—the registered households were now more than triple what they had been before.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ao reached Lian's capital at Pyongyang and inquired into the realm, he was told that its lands stretched more than a thousand li south of Liaodong, east to Seong Fortress, south to the Lesser Sea, and north to old Buyeo, with registered households now more than triple their former number.

sentences.zh: 魏時，其地東西二千里，南北一千餘里。

translations.literal: In the time of Wei its territory measured two thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times its domain measured two thousand li from east to west and more than a thousand li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 民皆土著，隨山谷而居，衣布帛及皮。

translations.literal: The people were all settled inhabitants who dwelt along the valleys and hills and wore cloth, silk, and hides.
translations.idiomatic: The people were sedentary, living along valleys and hillsides, and dressed in cloth, silk, and furs.

sentences.zh: 土田薄塉，蠶農不足以自供，故其人節飲食。

translations.literal: The soil was thin and poor; sericulture and farming were insufficient for self-sufficiency, and so the people were sparing in food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The land was thin and unproductive, and farming and sericulture could not fully sustain them, so the people were frugal in their eating and drinking.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫，好歌舞，夜則男女羣聚而戲，無貴賤之節，然潔淨自喜。

translations.literal: Their customs were licentious; they loved song and dance. At night men and women gathered in groups to sport without distinction of noble and base, yet they took pleasure in cleanliness.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were licentious and they loved song and dance; at night men and women gathered without regard to rank, yet they prided themselves on cleanliness.

sentences.zh: 其王好治宮室。

translations.literal: Their king loved to build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Their kings delighted in constructing palaces.

sentences.zh: 其官名有謁奢、太奢、大兄、小兄之號。

translations.literal: Among their official titles were Yeshe, Taishe, Da Xiong, and Xiao Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Their official titles included Yeshe, Taishe, Elder Brother, and Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 頭著折風，其形如弁，旁插鳥羽，貴賤有差。

translations.literal: On the head they wore a zhefeng, shaped like a cap, with bird feathers inserted at the sides according to differences of noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: They wore on the head a zhefeng cap shaped like a formal bonnet, with bird feathers at the sides in ranks that marked noble and common status.

sentences.zh: 立則反拱，跪拜曳一脚，行步如走。

translations.literal: When standing they folded their arms behind their backs; when kneeling and bowing they dragged one foot; in walking their gait was like running.
translations.idiomatic: When standing they clasped their hands behind their backs; when bowing they dragged one foot; and they walked with a quick, almost running step.

sentences.zh: 常以十月祭天，國中大會。

translations.literal: They regularly sacrificed to Heaven in the tenth month, when the whole state held a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the tenth month they sacrificed to Heaven in a great national assembly.

sentences.zh: 其公會，衣服皆錦繡，金銀以為飾。

translations.literal: At their public assemblies their garments were all brocade and embroidery, with gold and silver for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: At these assemblies the nobles wore brocade and embroidery adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 好蹲踞。

translations.literal: They liked to squat.
translations.idiomatic: They were fond of squatting.

sentences.zh: 食用俎几。

translations.literal: For eating they used stands and low tables.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from stands and low tables.

sentences.zh: 出三尺馬，云本朱蒙所乘，馬種即果下也。

translations.literal: They produced horses three feet in height; it is said that Jumong originally rode such a horse—the breed is the guoxia pony.
translations.idiomatic: They bred horses only three feet tall, said to be the same breed Jumong once rode—the guoxia pony.

sentences.zh: 後貢使相尋，歲致黃金二百斤，白銀四百斤。

translations.literal: Later tribute envoys followed one upon another, and each year they presented two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute missions came in steady succession, each year bringing two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 時馮文通率眾奔之，世祖遣散騎常侍封撥詔璉令送文通，璉上書稱當與文通俱奉王化，竟不送。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Wentong led his followers in flight to Goguryeo; Emperor Shizu sent Feng Bo, Regular Attendant Cavalier, with an edict ordering Lian to hand over Wentong. Lian memorialized that he and Wentong would together submit to royal civilization, but in the end he did not surrender him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Feng Wentong fled to Goguryeo with his followers. Emperor Shizu sent Feng Bo with an edict ordering Lian to extradite him. Lian replied that he and Wentong would together accept imperial rule, but in the end he refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，欲往討之，樂平王丕等議待後舉，世祖乃止，而文通亦尋為璉所殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was angry and wished to campaign against him; the Prince of Leping, Pi, and others argued that the expedition should wait for a later occasion, and the emperor desisted; before long Wentong was also killed by Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was enraged and prepared to march against him, but the Prince of Leping, Pi, and others urged delay, and the emperor held his hand. Before long Lian had Wentong killed as well.

sentences.zh: 後文明太后以顯祖六宮未備，敕璉令薦其女。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Wenming, because Emperor Xianzu's six palaces were not yet complete, ordered Lian to recommend his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Emperor Xianzu's inner palaces were not yet filled, Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Lian to present his daughter.

sentences.zh: 璉奉表，云女已出嫁，求以弟女應旨，朝廷許焉，乃遣安樂王真、尚書李敷等至境送幣。

translations.literal: Lian presented a memorial saying his daughter was already married and asking that his younger brother's daughter answer the imperial command; the court granted this, and then sent the Prince of Anle, Zhen, Minister Li Fu, and others to the border with betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Lian memorialized that his daughter was already married and asked that his younger brother's daughter be accepted instead. The court agreed and sent the Prince of Anle, Zhen, Minister Li Fu, and others to the border with betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 璉惑其左右之說，云朝廷昔與馮氏婚姻，未幾而滅其國，殷鑒不遠，宜以方便辭之。

translations.literal: Lian was swayed by those around him, who said that in former times the court had taken a Feng bride in marriage and before long had destroyed that state—the lesson was not far off, and he ought to decline by some expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was swayed by his advisers, who reminded him that when the court had once married a woman of the Feng clan, it had soon destroyed their kingdom—a warning too recent to ignore—and urged him to find some polite excuse.

sentences.zh: 璉遂上書妄稱女死。

translations.literal: Lian then memorialized falsely that the girl was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Lian then sent a false memorial claiming the girl had died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑其矯詐，又遣假散騎常侍程駿切責之，若女審死者，聽更選宗淑。

translations.literal: The court suspected deception and again sent Cheng Jun, Acting Regular Attendant Cavalier, to rebuke him sharply: if the girl were truly dead, he might select another clanswoman of good character.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspected fraud and sent Cheng Jun, Acting Regular Attendant Cavalier, to rebuke him sternly, adding that if the girl were truly dead he might choose another suitable woman of his clan.

sentences.zh: 璉云：「若天子恕其前愆，謹當奉詔。

translations.literal: Lian said, 'If the Son of Heaven will pardon my former fault, I shall respectfully obey the edict.'
translations.idiomatic: Lian replied, 'If the Son of Heaven will forgive my earlier offense, I shall respectfully obey.'

sentences.zh: 」會顯祖崩，乃止。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Xianzu died, and the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: But before anything further could be done, Emperor Xianzu died, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 至高祖時，璉貢獻倍前，其報賜亦稍加焉。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute was double what it had been before, and the gifts returned to him were likewise somewhat increased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute doubled, and the court's rewards in return grew somewhat as well.

sentences.zh: 時光州於海中得璉所遣詣蕭道成使餘奴等送闕，高祖詔責璉曰：「道成親殺其君，竊號江左，朕方欲興滅國於舊邦，繼絕世於劉氏，而卿越境外交，遠通篡賊，豈是藩臣守節之義！

translations.literal: At that time Guangzhou seized at sea Lian's envoys to Xiao Daocheng, Yu Nu and others, and sent them to court. Emperor Gaozu issued an edict rebuking Lian: 'Daocheng personally killed his sovereign and usurped the title south of the Yangzi. We are about to restore a destroyed state in its old domain and continue a severed line for the house of Liu, yet you cross your borders in foreign relations and reach out to a distant usurper—how is this the duty of a border vassal who keeps his integrity!'
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou then captured at sea Lian's envoys to Xiao Daocheng, including Yu Nu, and sent them to court. Emperor Gaozu rebuked Lian: 'Daocheng murdered his own sovereign and seized the title south of the Yangzi. We mean to restore a fallen kingdom and continue the Liu line, yet you send envoys across your border to treat with a distant usurper—is this how a loyal frontier vassal should behave?'

sentences.zh: 今不以一過掩卿舊款，即送還藩，其感恕思愆，祗承明憲，輯寧所部，動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Now we do not let one fault obscure your former sincerity. Return at once to your domain. Reflect on forgiveness and ponder your fault; respectfully accept the bright statutes, bring peace to your territories, and report your movements and repose.'
translations.idiomatic: We will not let this single fault efface your long record of loyalty. Return to your domain at once, reflect on our mercy, accept the imperial statutes, keep your lands in order, and report all you do.'

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，璉死，年百餘歲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died at an age of more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died at the age of more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉哀於東郊，遣謁者僕射李安上策贈車騎大將軍、太傅、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu observed mourning at the eastern suburb and sent Li An, Supervisor of Attendants, to present a patent of posthumous investiture as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu mourned him at the eastern suburb and sent Li An with a posthumous patent investing him as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Goguryeo, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 又遣大鴻臚拜璉孫雲使持節、都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾，又詔雲遣世子入朝，令及郊丘之禮。

translations.literal: He also sent the Grand Herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun as bearer of the credentials of authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Concurrent Protector of the Eastern Yi as Central Commandant, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo, granting robes, caps, garments, chariots, and banners; he also ordered Yun to send his heir to court in time for the suburban and Mount Tai sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the Grand Herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun with the same titles and to grant him robes, regalia, chariots, and banners. Yun was further ordered to send his heir to court in time for the suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 雲上書辭疾，惟遣其從叔升于隨使詣闕，嚴責之。

translations.literal: Yun memorialized pleading illness and sent only his younger uncle's son Shengyu with the envoy to court; the court rebuked him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: Yun pleaded illness in a memorial and sent only his cousin Shengyu with the embassy. The court rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常貢獻。

translations.literal: From this time tribute was presented every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute was sent every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 正始中，世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗，[2]悉弗進曰：「高麗係誠天極，累葉純誠，地產土毛，無愆王貢。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era Emperor Shizong received his envoy Ruixifu at the Eastern Hall. Ruixifu advanced and said, 'Goryeo has bound its loyalty to the pole of Heaven through successive generations of pure sincerity; the land produces local products, and there has been no shortfall in royal tribute.'
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Emperor Shizong received the envoy Ruixifu in the Eastern Hall. Ruixifu said, 'Goguryeo has bound its loyalty to Heaven through generations of sincere devotion. The land yields its native products, and we have never failed in tribute.'

sentences.zh: 但黃金出自夫餘，珂則涉羅所產。

translations.literal: But gold came from Buyeo, and ke-shell from Shero.
translations.idiomatic: But our gold came from Buyeo, and our ke-shells from Shero.

sentences.zh: 今夫餘為勿吉所逐，涉羅為百濟所并，國王臣雲惟繼絕之義，悉遷于境內。

translations.literal: Now Buyeo has been driven out by Wuji and Shero annexed by Baekje; King Yun, our subject, in the duty of continuing severed lines, has moved them all within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo has now been driven out by Wuji and Shero annexed by Baekje. Our king Yun, fulfilling the duty to preserve fallen states, has taken all their people within our borders.

sentences.zh: 二品所以不登王府，實兩賊是為。

translations.literal: The reason the second-grade tribute has not reached the imperial storehouse is truly because of these two enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the second-grade tribute has not reached the imperial treasury is solely these two aggressors.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「高麗世荷上將，專制海外，九夷黠虜，實得征之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said, 'Goryeo for generations has borne the imperial commission as chief general and held sole sway overseas; the crafty tribes among the nine Yi are in truth fit objects for your campaigns.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong replied, 'Goguryeo for generations has borne the imperial commission and ruled the eastern seas alone. These crafty tribes among the nine Yi are precisely what you are empowered to subdue.'

sentences.zh: 瓶罄罍耻，誰之咎也？

translations.literal: 'When the bottles are empty, the jars are shamed—whose fault is that?'
translations.idiomatic: 'When the bottles are empty, the jars are shamed—whose fault is that?'

sentences.zh: 昔方貢之愆，責在連率。

translations.literal: In former times, when regional tribute fell short, the blame lay with the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when tribute from the regions failed, the regional commander was held responsible.

sentences.zh: 卿宜宣朕旨於卿主，務盡威懷之略，揃披害羣，輯寧東裔，使二邑還復舊墟，土毛無失常貢也。」

translations.literal: You should proclaim Our intent to your lord: strive to exhaust the strategy of awe and kindness, sweep away the harmful tribes, bring peace to the eastern lands, and restore the two domains to their old sites so that local products may be offered without irregularity in tribute.'
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim Our intent to your king: employ both force and kindness, destroy these harmful peoples, pacify the eastern lands, restore the two domains to their former seats, and see that tribute flows again without interruption.'

sentences.zh: 神龜中，雲死，靈太后為舉哀於東堂，遣使策贈車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era Yun died; Empress Dowager Ling observed mourning for him at the Eastern Hall and sent envoys with a patent of posthumous investiture as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era Yun died. Empress Dowager Ling mourned him at the Eastern Hall and sent a posthumous patent investing him as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 又拜其世子安為安東將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: His heir An was also invested as General of the Pacified East, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His heir An was invested as General of the Pacified East, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 正光初，光州又於海中執得蕭衍所授安寧東將軍衣冠劍佩，及使人江法盛等，送於京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, Guangzhou again seized at sea the robes, cap, sword, and girdle ornaments of the General of the Pacified East conferred by Xiao Yan, together with his envoy Jiang Fasheng and others, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengguang, Guangzhou again captured at sea the regalia of General of the Pacified East that Xiao Yan had granted to An, together with the envoy Jiang Fasheng and his party, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 安死，子延立。

translations.literal: When An died, his son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When An died, his son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，詔加延使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign an edict added for Yan the titles bearer of the credentials of authority, Regular Attendant Cavalier, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong Commandery with a state-founding fief, and King of Goguryeo, granting robes, caps, garments, chariots, and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Chu, Yan was further invested as bearer of the credentials of authority, Regular Attendant Cavalier, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Goguryeo, with robes, regalia, chariots, and banners.

sentences.zh: 天平中，詔加延侍中、驃騎大將軍，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era an edict added for Yan the titles Attendant-in-Chief and General of Agile Cavalry; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was further made Attendant-in-Chief and General of Agile Cavalry; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 延死，子成立。

translations.literal: When Yan died, his son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died, his son Cheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 訖於武定末，其貢使無歲不至。

translations.literal: Down to the end of Wuding, tribute envoys came every year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the end of Wuding, tribute missions arrived every year without exception.

sentences.zh: 百濟國，其先出自夫餘。

translations.literal: The state of Baekje: its ancestors issued from Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Baekje traced its origins to Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 其國北去高句麗千餘里，處小海之南。

translations.literal: Its state lies more than a thousand li north of Goguryeo and stands south of the Lesser Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm lay more than a thousand li south of Goguryeo, on the southern shore of the Lesser Sea.

sentences.zh: 其民土著，地多下濕，率皆山居。

translations.literal: Its people were settled inhabitants; the land was largely low and wet, and for the most part they dwelt in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were sedentary; the land was low and marshy, and they mostly lived in the hills.

sentences.zh: 有五穀，其衣服飲食與高句麗同。

translations.literal: They had the five grains; their clothing and food were the same as Goguryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: They grew the five grains, and their dress and diet were the same as in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 延興二年，其王餘慶始遣使上表曰：「臣建國東極，豺狼隔路，雖世承靈化，莫由奉藩，瞻望雲闕，馳情罔極。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing, its king Yuqing first sent envoys with a memorial saying, 'Your subject founded his state at the eastern extremity; wolves block the road. Though we have received imperial grace generation after generation, we have had no means to submit as a vassal. Gazing toward the cloud-towered gate, my yearning knows no bound.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing, King Yuqing of Baekje sent his first embassy with a memorial: 'Your subject's kingdom stands at the eastern edge of the world, and wolves block the road between us. Though we have long received the court's grace, we have had no way to offer our submission. Gazing toward the imperial palace, my longing knows no limit.'

sentences.zh: 涼風微應，伏惟皇帝陛下協和天休，不勝係仰之情，謹遣私署冠軍將軍、駙馬都尉弗斯侯，長史餘禮，龍驤將軍、帶方太守、司馬張茂等投舫波阻，搜徑玄津，託命自然之運，遣進萬一之誠。

translations.literal: As the cool wind stirs slightly, I bow my head and consider that Your Majesty harmonizes with Heaven's favor; unable to bear the feeling of bound attachment, I respectfully send my privately appointed General of the Champions, Commandant of the Horse-Attendants Fusi Hou, Chief Clerk Yu Li, General of the Dragon Courser and Administrator of Daifang Zhang Mao, and others—casting their boats upon obstructing waves, seeking paths across the dark ford, trusting to the course of nature's workings—to present one ten-thousandth of our sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: As the cool wind rises, I humbly reflect that Your Majesty is in harmony with Heaven's favor. Unable to contain my devotion, I send my General of the Champions and Commandant of the Horse-Attendants Fusi Hou, Chief Clerk Yu Li, General of the Dragon Courser and Administrator of Daifang Zhang Mao, and others—they have braved the waves, found a path across the dark sea, and trust to Heaven's will to bear this faint token of our loyalty.

sentences.zh: 冀神祇垂感，皇靈洪覆，克達天庭，宣暢臣志，雖旦聞夕沒，永無餘恨。

translations.literal: I hope the spirits will extend their feeling, the imperial numen broadly cover us, that we may reach the heavenly court, give full voice to your subject's intent—even if we hear at dawn and perish at dusk, there will be no remaining regret.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits be moved and the imperial majesty extend over us, that we may reach the heavenly court and make our purpose known—even if we hear the reply at dawn and die at dusk, we shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「臣與高句麗源出夫餘，先世之時，篤崇舊款。

translations.literal: He also said, 'Your subject and Goguryeo both issued from Buyeo; in former generations we deeply honored our old friendship.'
translations.idiomatic: The memorial continued: 'Your subject and Goguryeo both spring from Buyeo, and in former ages we held each other in close friendship.'

sentences.zh: 其祖釗輕廢隣好，親率士眾，陵踐臣境。

translations.literal: Their ancestor Chao lightly cast aside neighborly friendship, personally led his warriors, and trampled across your subject's borders.
translations.idiomatic: But their ancestor Chao lightly broke that friendship, led his army in person, and ravaged our lands.

sentences.zh: 臣祖須整旅電邁，應機馳擊，矢石暫交，梟斬釗首。

translations.literal: Your subject's ancestor Xu swiftly arrayed his troops like lightning, struck as opportunity allowed, and after arrows and stones had briefly crossed, beheaded Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's ancestor Xu mustered his troops and struck like lightning; after only a brief clash of arms he took Chao's head.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，莫敢南顧。

translations.literal: From that time onward none dared look southward again.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward none of them dared turn south again.

sentences.zh: 自馮氏數終，餘燼奔竄，醜類漸盛，遂見陵逼，構怨連禍，三十餘載，財殫力竭，轉自孱踧。

translations.literal: Since the Feng clan's fate was exhausted, the remaining embers fled in disorder; the ugly sort gradually grew strong, and we came to suffer their oppression. Grievance piled upon calamity for more than thirty years; wealth was spent and strength exhausted, and we grew ever more weak and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Feng fell, its remnants fled to us, but their enemies grew stronger still and pressed us hard. For more than thirty years grievance followed disaster, until our wealth was spent and our strength exhausted and we grew ever weaker.

sentences.zh: 若天慈曲矜，遠及無外，速遣一將，來救臣國，當奉送鄙女，執掃後宮，并遣子弟，牧圉外廐。

translations.literal: If Heaven's kindness bends with compassion, reaching far to exclude none, and you swiftly send a general to rescue your subject's state, I shall present my humble daughter to sweep the inner palace, and also send younger kinsmen to tend the outer stables.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty in Heaven's mercy extends his care even to the farthest lands and quickly sends a general to save my kingdom, I shall offer my humble daughter to serve in the inner palace and send my sons to tend your outer stables.

sentences.zh: 尺壤匹夫不敢自有。

translations.literal: Not a foot of soil or a single commoner would I dare hold for myself.
translations.idiomatic: Not a foot of my soil nor a single subject would I keep for myself.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「今璉有罪，國自魚肉，大臣強族，戮殺無已，罪盈惡積，民庶崩離。

translations.literal: He also said, 'Now Lian is guilty; the state is being carved like fish on a board. Great ministers and powerful clans slaughter without end; crimes overflow and wickedness accumulates, and the common people are collapsing in flight.'
translations.idiomatic: The memorial continued: 'King Lian is guilty; his realm is being carved up like fish on a cutting board. Powerful ministers and great clans slaughter without end; crime and wickedness have piled high, and the people are fleeing in disorder.'

sentences.zh: 是滅亡之期，假手之秋也。

translations.literal: This is the season of extinction, the autumn in which to borrow another's hand.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour of their destruction—the moment to strike with another's hand.

sentences.zh: 且馮族士馬，有鳥畜之戀；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Feng clan's warriors and horses still hold the longing of birds for their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Feng warriors and horses still yearn for their homeland as birds yearn for their nests.

sentences.zh: 樂浪諸郡，懷首丘之心。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Lelang harbor hearts that turn toward their old mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Lelang commanderies still turn their hearts toward their ancestral hills.

sentences.zh: 天威一舉，有征無戰。

translations.literal: When Heaven's majesty moves once, there will be campaigns without battles.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty's majesty moves once, you will conquer without fighting.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，志效畢力，當率所統，承風響應。

translations.literal: Though your subject is not clever, he aspires to exhaust his strength; he will lead those under his command to answer to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I will give all my strength and lead my forces to answer your call.

sentences.zh: 且高麗不義，逆詐非一，外慕隗囂藩卑之辭，內懷兇禍豕突之行。

translations.literal: Moreover Goguryeo is unrighteous; its treachery and deceit are not one alone—outwardly it admires the humble words of a frontier vassal like Wei Xiao, inwardly it harbors the violent rush of a rampaging boar.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo is faithless; its treacheries are many. Outwardly it flatters like a humble frontier vassal; inwardly it schemes like a wild boar on the rampage.

sentences.zh: 或南通劉氏，或北約蠕蠕，共相脣齒，謀陵王略。

translations.literal: Sometimes it allies with the Liu house in the south, sometimes it treaties with the Rouran in the north; they are lip and teeth to each other, plotting to encroach upon the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: It allies now with the Liu in the south, now with the Rouran in the north, acting as mutual support in a plot to threaten the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯至聖，致罰丹水；

translations.literal: In former times even the supremely sage Emperor Yao of Tang punished the Dan River tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Even the sage Emperor Yao of antiquity punished the tribes of the Dan River.

sentences.zh: 孟常稱仁，不捨塗詈。

translations.literal: Mengchang was called humane, yet he did not spare those who cursed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang was famed for humanity, yet he did not spare those who reviled him in the streets.

sentences.zh: 涓流之水，宜早壅塞，今若不取，將貽後悔。

translations.literal: A trickling stream should be dammed early; if you do not take it now, you will leave regret for later.
translations.idiomatic: A trickling stream should be stopped early; if you do not act now, you will regret it later.

sentences.zh: 去庚辰年後，臣西界小石山北國海中見屍十餘，并得衣器鞍勒，視之非高麗之物，後聞乃是王人來降臣國。

translations.literal: After the gengchen year, on the northern sea beyond the Small Stone Mountain on my western border, more than ten corpses were seen, together with clothing, vessels, and saddle trappings; viewing them, they were not Goguryeo goods. Later I heard they were men of the king's court coming to surrender to your subject's state.
translations.idiomatic: After the gengchen year, on the northern sea beyond Small Stone Mountain on my western frontier, more than ten corpses were found with clothing, gear, and saddlery that were plainly not Goguryeo goods. I later learned they were men of your court fleeing to my kingdom.

sentences.zh: 長蛇隔路，以沉于海，雖未委當，深懷憤恚。

translations.literal: The long serpent blocked the road and they sank in the sea; though the matter is not yet fully verified, I harbor deep indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, like a great serpent, barred their way and they perished at sea. Though the facts are not yet fully known, my anger runs deep.

sentences.zh: 昔宋戮申舟，楚莊徒跣；

translations.literal: In former times when Song killed Shen Zhou, King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Song killed Shen Zhou, King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot in mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 鷂撮放鳩，信陵不食。

translations.literal: When the sparrow hawk seized the dove, Lord Xinling refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the hawk seized the dove, Lord Xinling would not eat.

sentences.zh: 克敵建名，美隆無已。

translations.literal: To defeat the enemy and establish one's name—such glory knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: To defeat the enemy and win renown—such glory is everlasting.

sentences.zh: 夫以區區偏鄙，猶慕萬代之信，況陛下合氣天地，勢傾山海，豈令小竪，跨塞天逵。

translations.literal: If even our petty, remote corner still cherishes faith lasting ten thousand generations, how much more should Your Majesty, who harmonizes with Heaven and earth and whose power overturns mountains and seas, permit a petty chieftain to block the heavenly road!
translations.idiomatic: If even our small, remote kingdom still honors eternal faith, how much more should Your Majesty, who unites with Heaven and earth and whose power shakes mountains and seas, allow a petty chieftain to block the imperial highway!

sentences.zh: 今上所得鞍一，以為實驗。」

translations.literal: The saddle now presented above is offered as proof.'
translations.idiomatic: I present the saddle found above as proof.'

sentences.zh: 顯祖以其僻遠，冒險朝獻，禮遇優厚，遣使者邵安與其使俱還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu, because they were remote and had braved danger to come in tribute, treated them with exceptional courtesy and sent the envoy Shao An to return with their embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu, impressed that they had braved the distant seas to offer tribute, received them with exceptional honor and sent Shao An to escort their embassy home.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得表聞之，無恙甚善。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'We have received your memorial and learned of it; that you are well is very good.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'We have received your memorial and are pleased to learn that you are well.'

sentences.zh: 卿在東隅，處五服之外，不遠山海，歸誠魏闕，欣嘉至意，用戢于懷。

translations.literal: You stand in the eastern corner, beyond the five domains, yet not far from mountains and seas you have turned your hearts to the Wei court. We rejoice in your utmost sincerity and have stilled it in Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the eastern edge of the world, beyond the five domains, yet despite mountains and seas you have turned your hearts to the Wei court. We rejoice in your sincerity and hold it close.

sentences.zh: 朕承萬世之業，君臨四海，統御羣生。

translations.literal: We inherit the enterprise of ten thousand generations, rule over the four seas, and govern all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: We inherit the enterprise of ten thousand generations, rule the four seas, and govern all living beings.

sentences.zh: 今宇內清一，八表歸義，襁負而至者不可稱數，風俗之和，士馬之盛，皆餘禮等親所聞見。

translations.literal: Now within the realm there is unity; the eight directions return to righteousness. Those who come swaddled on the back are beyond counting. The harmony of customs and the abundance of warriors and horses are all things Yu Li and the others have themselves seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm there is peace; the eight directions submit. Countless peoples arrive bearing children on their backs. The harmony of customs and the strength of armies are things your envoys have themselves witnessed.

sentences.zh: 卿與高麗不穆，屢致陵犯，苟能順義，守之以仁，亦何憂於寇讎也。

translations.literal: You and Goguryeo are not at peace and have repeatedly suffered invasion. If you can follow righteousness and guard it with humanity, what need is there to worry about enemies?
translations.idiomatic: You and Goguryeo are at odds and have suffered repeated invasions. If you uphold righteousness and govern with humanity, what enemy need you fear?

sentences.zh: 前所遣使，浮海以撫荒外之國，從來積年，往而不返，存亡達否，未能審悉。

translations.literal: The envoys formerly dispatched crossed the sea to comfort states beyond the wilds; for years they have gone and not returned, and whether they live or die, succeed or fail, We have been unable to ascertain fully.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys We once sent across the sea to the outer lands have for years gone forth and not returned, and We have been unable to learn whether they live or die.

sentences.zh: 卿所送鞍，比校舊乘，非中國之物。

translations.literal: The saddle you sent, compared with Our old mounts, is not a product of China.
translations.idiomatic: The saddle you sent, compared with Our own mounts, is plainly not of Chinese make.

sentences.zh: 不可以疑似之事，以生必然之過。

translations.literal: One must not, on the basis of doubtful matters, give rise to certain accusations.
translations.idiomatic: You must not turn doubtful matters into certain accusations.

sentences.zh: 經略權要，已具別旨。

translations.literal: The essentials of strategy and power have already been set forth in separate instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of strategy have been set forth in separate instructions.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「知高麗阻強，侵軼卿土，修先君之舊怨，棄息民之大德，兵交累載，難結荒邊。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 'We know that Goguryeo, relying on its strength, encroaches upon your lands, pursues old grievances of former rulers, and abandons the great virtue of giving rest to the people. Arms have clashed for many years and the distant border is hard to pacify.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: 'We know Goguryeo, relying on its strength, encroaches on your lands, nurses old royal grievances, and neglects the welfare of its people. War has dragged on for years and the frontier remains unsettled.'

sentences.zh: 使兼申胥之誠，國有楚越之急，乃應展義扶微，乘機電舉。

translations.literal: It would make you combine the loyalty of Shen Xu and the urgency of Chu and Yue; you ought to display righteousness in supporting the weak and strike like lightning seizing opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: You would combine the loyalty of Shen Xu with the urgency of Chu and Yue; you should aid the weak in righteousness and strike when opportunity comes like lightning.

sentences.zh: 但以高麗稱藩先朝，供職日久，於彼雖有自昔之釁，於國未有犯令之愆。

translations.literal: But Goguryeo has called itself a vassal to former courts and long performed its duties; though it has old offenses on its side, toward Our state it has not yet committed a breach of command.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Goguryeo has long been a vassal of former courts and performed its duties faithfully; though it has old offenses, it has not yet violated Our commands.

sentences.zh: 卿使命始通，便求致伐，尋討事會，理亦未周。

translations.literal: Your mission has only just opened relations, yet you immediately ask for a punitive expedition; searching into the circumstances, the principle is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your embassy has only just arrived, yet you already ask for war; considered carefully, the matter is not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 故往年遣禮等至平壤，欲驗其由狀。

translations.literal: Therefore in former years We sent Li and others to Pyongyang to verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We sent Li and others to Pyongyang last year to investigate the facts.

sentences.zh: 然高麗奏請頻煩，辭理俱詣，行人不能抑其請，司法無以成其責，故聽其所啟，詔禮等還。

translations.literal: Yet Goguryeo's memorials were frequent and its arguments all reached the mark; the traveling envoy could not restrain its petitions, and the judicial offices could not fix its guilt, so We allowed what it requested and ordered Li and others to return.
translations.idiomatic: But Goguryeo's petitions were frequent and its arguments persuasive; Our envoy could not refuse its requests, and the courts could not establish its guilt, so We allowed its pleas and recalled Li and his party.

sentences.zh: 若今復違旨，則過咎益露，後雖自陳，無所逃罪，然後興師討之，於義為得。

translations.literal: If now it again disobeys Our command, its faults will be all the more exposed; later, even if it pleads for itself, there will be no escaping punishment—then to raise troops and chastise it will be right in principle.
translations.idiomatic: If it now disobeys Our command again, its guilt will be plain for all to see; even if it pleads later, it cannot escape punishment—then to march against it will be just.

sentences.zh: 九夷之國，世居海外，道暢則奉藩，惠戢則保境，故羈縻著於前典，楛貢曠於歲時。

translations.literal: The states of the nine Yi dwell beyond the seas generation after generation; when the Way prevails they submit as vassals, when kindness is at rest they guard their borders—thus tethering and bridling are recorded in former canons, and tribute of arrow-shafts has sometimes lapsed with the years.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of the nine Yi have always lived beyond the seas; when the Way prevails they submit, when kindness rests they guard their borders. Thus former canons record their tethering, though tribute has sometimes lapsed.

sentences.zh: 卿備陳強弱之形，具列往代之迹，俗殊事異，擬貺乖衷，洪規大略，其致猶在。

translations.literal: You have fully set forth the forms of strength and weakness and listed the traces of former ages; customs differ and affairs vary, and your proposed gifts miss the mark, yet the great design and broad outline—their intent remains.
translations.idiomatic: You have fully described their strength and weakness and recounted former ages; customs differ and your comparisons miss the mark, yet the broad design you propose still holds.

sentences.zh: 今中夏平一，宇內無虞，每欲陵威東極，懸旌域表，拯荒黎於偏方，舒皇風於遠服。

translations.literal: Now the central realm is unified and within the four seas there is no worry. We constantly wish to display Our majesty at the eastern extremity, plant Our banners beyond the borders, rescue the wild peoples in remote corners, and spread the imperial wind to distant domains.
translations.idiomatic: Now the central realm is united and the realm is at peace. We long to display Our majesty in the far east, plant Our banners beyond the borders, rescue distant peoples, and spread imperial civilization to the outer lands.

sentences.zh: 良由高麗即敍，未及卜征。

translations.literal: It is truly because Goguryeo is for the moment submissive that We have not yet chosen the day for campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Goguryeo is for the moment submissive have We not yet chosen a day for campaign.

sentences.zh: 今若不從詔旨，則卿之來謀，載協朕意，元戎啟行，將不云遠。

translations.literal: If now you do not follow the edict's intent, then your coming counsel accords with Our mind; the main army will set forth—it will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: If you now follow Our edict, your counsel accords with Our mind; the main army will march—and not long from now.

sentences.zh: 便可豫率同興，具以待事，時遣報使，速究彼情。

translations.literal: You may beforehand lead your allies to rise together and make ready to await the affair; send reporting envoys in season to investigate their situation quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare your allies to rise together and stand ready; send envoys in good time to report on their situation.

sentences.zh: 師舉之日，卿為鄉導之首，大捷之後，又受元功之賞，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: On the day the army is raised you shall be chief guide; after the great victory you will again receive reward for the highest merit—is this not good?
translations.idiomatic: When the army marches you shall lead the way; after the great victory you shall receive the highest reward—is that not well?

sentences.zh: 所獻錦布海物雖不悉達，明卿至心。

translations.literal: The brocade, cloth, and sea products presented, though not all arrived, show your utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Though not all the brocade, cloth, and sea products you sent arrived, your utmost sincerity is clear.

sentences.zh: 今賜雜物如別。

translations.literal: Now miscellaneous gifts are granted as listed separately.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous gifts are now granted as listed separately.

sentences.zh: 」又詔璉護送安等。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Lian to escort An and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Lian to escort An and his party.

sentences.zh: 安等至高句麗，璉稱昔與餘慶有讎，不令東過，安等於是皆還。

translations.literal: When An and the others reached Goguryeo, Lian said that in former times he had a feud with Yuqing and would not let them pass eastward; An and the others therefore all returned.
translations.idiomatic: When An and his party reached Goguryeo, Lian claimed an old feud with Yuqing and refused to let them pass eastward, so they all turned back.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔切責之。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 五年，使安等從東萊浮海，賜餘慶璽書，褒其誠節。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, An and the others were sent from Donglai across the sea, and an imperial letter with the seal was granted to Yuqing praising his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, An and his party set out from Donglai by sea, bearing an imperial letter with the seal praising Yuqing's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 安等至海濱，遇風飄蕩，竟不達而還。

translations.literal: When An and the others reached the seashore, they met winds and were driven about, and in the end did not arrive but returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the seashore they were scattered by storms and never reached Baekje, returning empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 勿吉國，在高句麗北，舊肅慎國也。

translations.literal: The state of Wuji lies north of Goguryeo; it is the old land of the Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Wuji lay north of Goguryeo; it was the old land of the Sushen.

sentences.zh: 邑落各自有長，不相總一。

translations.literal: Each settlement had its own chief and they were not united under one ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Each settlement had its own chief and they were not united under one ruler.

sentences.zh: 其人勁悍，於東夷最強。

translations.literal: Its people were fierce and strong—the most powerful among the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were fierce and strong—the most powerful among the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 言語獨異。

translations.literal: Their language was unique.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was unique.

sentences.zh: 常輕豆莫婁等國，諸國亦患之。

translations.literal: They regularly looked down on the states of Doumolou and others; the various states also feared them.
translations.idiomatic: They regularly looked down on Doumolou and neighboring states, who in turn feared them.

sentences.zh: 去洛五千里。

translations.literal: It was five thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自和龍北二百餘里有善玉山，山北行十三日至祁黎山，又北行七日至如洛瓌水，水廣里餘，又北行十五日至太魯水，又東北行十八日到其國。

translations.literal: Two hundred-odd li north of Helong was Mount Shanyu; thirteen days' travel north from the mountain brought one to Mount Qili; seven days further north to the Ruluohui River, more than a li wide; fifteen days further north to the Tailu River; eighteen days northeast to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred-odd li north of Helong stood Mount Shanyu; thirteen days' march north brought one to Mount Qili, seven days more to the Ruluohui River, more than a li across, fifteen days more to the Tailu River, and eighteen days northeast to their capital.

sentences.zh: 國有大水，闊三里餘，名速末水。

translations.literal: The state had a great river more than three li wide, named the Sumo River.
translations.idiomatic: Their land had a great river more than three li wide called the Sumo River.

sentences.zh: 其地下濕，築城穴居，屋形似塚，開口於上，以梯出入。

translations.literal: The ground was low and wet; they built walled settlements and dwelt in caves. Their houses resembled mounds, with openings above and ladders for entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: The ground was low and wet; they built walled settlements and lived in pit-dwellings shaped like mounds, entering and leaving by ladder through an opening in the roof.

sentences.zh: 其國無牛，有車馬，佃則偶耕，車則步推。

translations.literal: Their state had no cattle but had chariots and horses; for farming they plowed in pairs, and for carts they pushed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: They had no cattle but kept horses and chariots; they plowed in pairs for farming and pushed carts on foot.

sentences.zh: 有粟及麥穄，菜則有葵。

translations.literal: They had millet and hulled wheat; for vegetables they had mallow.
translations.idiomatic: They grew millet and wheat, and mallow among vegetables.

sentences.zh: 水氣醎凝，鹽生樹上，亦有鹽池。

translations.literal: Water vapor was salty and congealed; salt grew on trees, and there were also salt pools.
translations.idiomatic: Salt formed on trees from congealed brine, and there were salt pools as well.

sentences.zh: 多猪無羊。

translations.literal: They had many pigs but no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They kept many pigs but no sheep.

sentences.zh: 嚼米醞酒，飲能至醉。

translations.literal: They chewed rice to brew wine; drinking it, one could become thoroughly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: They chewed rice to brew wine strong enough to bring on deep drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 婦人則布裙，男子猪犬皮裘。

translations.literal: Women wore cloth skirts; men wore furs of pig and dog.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore cloth skirts; men wore furs of pig and dog skin.

sentences.zh: 初婚之夕，男就女家執女乳而罷，便以為定，仍為夫婦。

translations.literal: On the first night of marriage the man went to the woman's house, grasped her breast, and then stopped; this was taken as the bond, and they became husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night the groom went to the bride's house, touched her breast, and the match was sealed; they then became husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 俗以人溺洗手面。

translations.literal: By custom they washed hands and face with human urine.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they washed their hands and faces with human urine.

sentences.zh: 頭插虎豹尾。

translations.literal: They inserted tiger and leopard tails in their hair.
translations.idiomatic: They wore tiger and leopard tails in their hair.

sentences.zh: 善射獵，弓長三尺，箭長尺二寸，以石為鏃。

translations.literal: They were skilled at shooting and hunting; bows were three feet long, arrows a foot and two inches, with stone points.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at hunting; their bows were three feet long, their arrows a foot and two inches, tipped with stone.

sentences.zh: 其父母春夏死，立埋之，冢上作屋，不令雨濕；

translations.literal: When parents died in spring or summer they were buried at once and a house was built on the mound so rain would not wet them.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died in spring or summer they were buried at once and a shelter built over the mound to keep off the rain.

sentences.zh: 若秋冬，以其屍捕貂，貂食其肉，多得之。

translations.literal: If in autumn or winter, they used the corpse to trap sable; the sable ate the flesh and many were caught.
translations.idiomatic: If death came in autumn or winter, they used the corpse to bait sable traps; the sable ate the flesh and many were caught.

sentences.zh: 常七八月造毒藥傅箭鏃，射禽獸，中者便死，煮藥毒氣亦能殺人。

translations.literal: Regularly in the seventh or eighth month they made poison, smeared it on arrow points, and shot birds and beasts; those hit died at once, and the vapor from boiling the drug could also kill men.
translations.idiomatic: Each seventh or eighth month they made poison for arrow points; beasts struck died at once, and even the vapor from boiling the poison could kill a man.

sentences.zh: 國南有徒太山，魏言「大白」，有虎豹羆狼害人，人不得山上溲汙，行逕山者，皆以物盛。

translations.literal: South of the state was Mount Taitai—in Wei speech 'Great White'—with tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves that harmed people. One might not relieve oneself on the mountain; those who traveled paths on the mountain all carried vessels.
translations.idiomatic: South of their land stood Mount Taitai—'Great White' in Wei speech—with tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves. No one might relieve himself on the mountain; travelers carried vessels for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 去延興中，遣使乙力支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era they sent the envoy Yilizhi to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing they sent the envoy Yilizhi to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太和初，又貢馬五百匹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe they again presented five hundred horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe they again presented five hundred horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 乙力支稱：初發其國，乘船泝難河西上，至太𣳅河，沉船於水，南出陸行，渡洛孤水，從契丹西界達和龍。

translations.literal: Yilizhi stated: when they first set out from their state they sailed up the Nanshui River by boat to the Tai River, sank the boat in the water, continued south by land, crossed the Luogu River, and reached Helong by way of the western border of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Yilizhi reported that they had sailed up the Nanshui River, scuttled their boat at the Tai River, continued overland south, crossed the Luogu River, and reached Helong by the Khitan western border.

sentences.zh: 自云其國先破高句麗十落，密共百濟謀從水道并力取高句麗，遣乙力支奉使大國，請其可否。

translations.literal: They themselves said their state had first broken ten settlements of Goguryeo and secretly plotted with Baekje to take Goguryeo by water route with combined strength; they sent Yilizhi to the great state to ask whether this was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: They said their state had already overrun ten Goguryeo settlements and were secretly plotting with Baekje to attack Goguryeo by sea; Yilizhi was sent to ask the great state's permission.

sentences.zh: 詔敕三國同是藩附，宜共和順，勿相侵擾。

translations.literal: An edict commanded: the three states are alike frontier vassals and should live in harmony together; do not encroach upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded that all three states were frontier vassals and should live in harmony without encroaching on one another.

sentences.zh: 乙力支乃還。

translations.literal: Yilizhi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yilizhi then returned.

sentences.zh: 從其來道，取得本船，汎達其國。

translations.literal: Following the route by which he had come, he recovered his original boat and sailed back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: By the route he had come he recovered his original boat and sailed home.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣使侯尼支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they again sent the envoy Hounizhi to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they again sent the envoy Hounizhi to court.

sentences.zh: 明年復入貢。

translations.literal: The following year they again entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其傍有大莫盧國、覆鍾國、莫多回國、庫婁國、素和國、具弗伏國、[3]匹黎尒國、拔大何國、[4]郁羽陵國、庫伏真國、魯婁國、羽真侯國，前後各遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Nearby were the states of Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu, Pilier, Badahé, Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou; each in turn sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby lay Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu, Pilier, Badahé, Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou, each of which sent envoys to court in turn.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，勿吉復遣使貢楛矢方物於京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Wuji again sent envoys presenting arrow-shafts and local products to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Wuji again sent envoys with arrow-shafts and local products to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十七年，又遣使人婆非等五百餘人朝獻。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they again sent the envoy Renpo Fei and more than five hundred others to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year they sent the envoy Renpo Fei and more than five hundred others to court.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，復遣使俟力歸等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others to court.

sentences.zh: 自此迄于正光，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: From this down to Zhengguang, tribute envoys followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: From then until Zhengguang, tribute missions came in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 爾後，中國紛擾，頗或不至。

translations.literal: Afterward China was in turmoil and they sometimes did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when China fell into turmoil, they sometimes failed to come.

sentences.zh: 興和二年六月，遣使石久云等貢方物，至於武定不絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent the envoy Shi Jiuyun and others with local products; down to Wuding they did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent Shi Jiuyun and others with local products, and missions continued without break down to Wuding.

sentences.zh: 失韋國，在勿吉北千里，去洛六千里。

translations.literal: The state of Shiwei lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 路出和龍北千餘里，入契丹國，又北行十日至啜水，又北行三日有蓋水，又北行三日有犢了山，其山高大，周回三百餘里，又北行三日有大水名屈利，又北行三日至刃水，又北行五日到其國。

translations.literal: The route passed more than a thousand li north of Helong, entered the Khitan state, ten days north to the Chuo River, three days north to the Gai River, three days north to Mount Duliao—high and great, circling more than three hundred li—three days north to the great river named Quli, three days north to the Ren River, five days north to their state.
translations.idiomatic: The route ran more than a thousand li north of Helong through Khitan territory: ten days north to the Chuo River, three days to the Gai River, three days to great Mount Duliao, three hundred li around, three days to the Quli River, three days to the Ren River, and five days north to their capital.

sentences.zh: 有大水從北而來，廣四里餘，名㮈水。

translations.literal: A great river came from the north, more than four li wide, named the Nu River.
translations.idiomatic: A great river more than four li wide flowed from the north, called the Nu River.

sentences.zh: 國土下濕。

translations.literal: The land was low and wet.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low and marshy.

sentences.zh: 語與庫莫奚、契丹、豆莫婁國同。

translations.literal: Their speech was the same as that of the Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou states.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was the same as that of the Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou.

sentences.zh: 頗有粟麥及穄，唯食猪魚，養牛馬，俗又無羊。

translations.literal: They had considerable millet, wheat, and hulled grain; they ate only pork and fish, raised cattle and horses, and by custom had no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They grew millet, wheat, and hulled grain; they ate pork and fish, raised cattle and horses, and had no sheep.

sentences.zh: 夏則城居，冬逐水草。

translations.literal: In summer they dwelt in walled settlements; in winter they followed water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they lived in walled settlements; in winter they followed pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 亦多貂皮。

translations.literal: They also had many sable pelts.
translations.idiomatic: They also had many sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 丈夫索髮。

translations.literal: The men wore their hair loose.
translations.idiomatic: The men wore their hair loose.

sentences.zh: 用角弓，其箭尤長。

translations.literal: They used horn bows; their arrows were especially long.
translations.idiomatic: They used horn bows and especially long arrows.

sentences.zh: 女婦束髮，作叉手髻。

translations.literal: Women bound their hair and made a forked-hand bun.
translations.idiomatic: Women bound their hair in a forked-hand bun.

sentences.zh: 其國少竊盜，盜一徵三，殺人者責馬三百匹。

translations.literal: Their state had little theft; for one theft three were levied, and for killing a man three hundred horses were exacted.
translations.idiomatic: Theft was rare; one thief paid for three, and a murderer was fined three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 男女悉衣白鹿皮襦袴。

translations.literal: Men and women alike wore jackets and trousers of white deerskin.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike dressed in white deerskin jackets and trousers.

sentences.zh: 有麴釀酒。

translations.literal: They had wine brewed from yeast.
translations.idiomatic: They brewed wine from grain mash.

sentences.zh: 俗愛赤珠，為婦人飾，穿挂於頸，以多為貴，女不得此，乃至不嫁。

translations.literal: By custom they loved red pearls as women's ornament, strung and hung at the neck; the more one had, the more honored—and a girl who did not obtain them might not marry.
translations.idiomatic: They prized red pearls as women's ornaments, hung about the neck; the more pearls, the higher the status, and a girl without them might not marry.

sentences.zh: 父母死，男女眾哭三年，屍則置於林樹之上。

translations.literal: When parents died, men and women wailed together for three years; the corpse was placed in the forest upon the trees.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, the whole family mourned for three years and placed the body in the forest treetops.

sentences.zh: 武定二年四月，始遣使張焉豆伐等獻其方物，迄武定末，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Wuding they first sent the envoy Zhang Yandoufa and others to present local products; down to the end of Wuding tribute envoys followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Wuding they first sent Zhang Yandoufa and others with local products; tribute missions continued without break until the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 豆莫婁國，在勿吉國北千里，去洛六千里，舊北扶餘也。

translations.literal: The state of Doumolou lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang; it was old Northern Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: Doumolou lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang; it was the old territory of Northern Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 在失韋之東，東至於海，方二千里。

translations.literal: It lay east of Shiwei, reaching the sea in the east, two thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: It lay east of Shiwei, extending to the sea, covering two thousand square li.

sentences.zh: 其人土著，有宮室倉庫。

translations.literal: Its people were settled inhabitants and had palaces and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were sedentary and had palaces and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 多山陵廣澤，於東夷之域最為平敞。

translations.literal: There were many hills and broad marshes; among the lands of the Eastern Yi it was the most level and open.
translations.idiomatic: Its land had many hills and broad marshes and was the most level and open among the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 地宜五穀，不生五果。

translations.literal: The soil was suited to the five grains but did not produce the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The soil grew the five grains but not orchard fruits.

sentences.zh: 其人長大，性強勇，謹厚，不寇抄。

translations.literal: Its people were tall, by nature strong and brave, careful and honest, and did not raid or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were tall, brave, prudent, and honest, and did not raid or plunder.

sentences.zh: 其君長皆以六畜名官，邑落有豪帥。

translations.literal: Their rulers and chiefs all took official names from the six domestic animals; in the settlements there were powerful leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs named their offices after the six domestic animals, and each settlement had powerful leaders.

sentences.zh: 飲食亦用俎豆。

translations.literal: For food and drink they also used stands and dishes.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from stands and dishes as well.

sentences.zh: 有麻布衣，制類高麗而幅大，其國大人，以金銀飾之。

translations.literal: They had hemp cloth garments, made like Goguryeo's but broader in the weave; the great men of the state adorned them with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: They wore hemp cloth like Goguryeo's but broader in weave; nobles adorned their garments with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴急，殺人者死，沒其家人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Punishments were severe and urgent: murderers were put to death and their families were confiscated as male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was harsh: murderers were executed and their families enslaved.

sentences.zh: 俗淫，尤惡妬婦，妬者殺之，尸其國南山上至腐。

translations.literal: Their customs were licentious and they especially hated jealous wives; jealous women were killed and their corpses exposed on the southern mountain of the state until they rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were licentious and they hated jealous wives, whom they killed and left on the southern mountain until the bodies rotted.

sentences.zh: 女家欲得，輸牛馬乃與之。

translations.literal: If the bride's family wished to have her, cattle and horses were paid over before she was given.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's family received cattle and horses before giving her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 或言本穢貊之地也。

translations.literal: Some say it was originally the land of the Filthy Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that it was originally Mo territory.

sentences.zh: 地豆于國，[5]在失韋西千餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Didouyu lay more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Didouyu lay more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊，出名馬，皮為衣服，無五穀，惟食肉酪。

translations.literal: It had many cattle and sheep and produced famous horses; skins served for clothing. It had no grain and ate only meat and curds.
translations.idiomatic: It had many cattle and sheep and famed horses; people dressed in hides and ate only meat and dairy, with no grain.

sentences.zh: 延興二年八月，遣使朝貢，至于太和六年，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yanxing they sent envoys to court with tribute; down to the sixth year of Taihe tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yanxing's second year they sent tribute envoys, and missions continued without break until Taihe's sixth year.

sentences.zh: 十四年，頻來犯塞，高祖詔征西大將軍、陽平王頤擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they repeatedly came to raid the frontier; Emperor Gaozu ordered the General Who Conquers the West, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they repeatedly raided the frontier; Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Yangping, Yi, to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 自後時朝京師，迄武定末，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: Afterward they sometimes came to the capital; down to the end of Wuding tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sometimes visited the capital, and tribute missions continued until the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚國之先，東部宇文之別種也。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Kumo Xi state were a separate branch of the Eastern Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi were a branch of the Eastern Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 初為慕容元真所破，遺落者竄匿松漠之間。

translations.literal: At first they were broken by Murong Yuanzhen; the survivors fled and hid among the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yuanzhen first defeated them, and the survivors fled into the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 其民不潔淨，而善射獵，好為寇鈔。

translations.literal: Their people were not clean, yet were skilled at shooting and hunting and loved to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They were unclean in their habits but skilled hunters who loved to raid and plunder.

sentences.zh: 登國三年，太祖親自出討，至弱洛水南，大破之，獲其四部落，馬牛羊豕十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dengguo the Taizu personally campaigned against them, reaching south of the Ruoluo River, where he routed them utterly, taking four of their tribes and more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, sheep, and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: In Dengguo's third year Taizu campaigned in person to the Ruoluo River, routed them utterly, took four tribes, and seized more than a hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此羣狄諸種不識德義，互相侵盜，有犯王略，故往征之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, 'These many Di tribes do not know virtue and righteousness; they rob one another, and when they offend against the royal domain We go to chastise them.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'These tribes know neither virtue nor duty; they rob one another, and when they offend the realm We chastise them.'

sentences.zh: 且鼠竊狗盜，何足為患。

translations.literal: Moreover, rats stealing and dogs prowling—how can they be a source of trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Rats and dogs stealing in the night—what harm can they do?'

sentences.zh: 今中州大亂，吾先平之，然後張其威懷，則無所不服矣。

translations.literal: Now the central realm is in great disorder; We shall first pacify it, and then extend Our majesty and kindness, and none will fail to submit.'
translations.idiomatic: The central realm is in chaos; We shall pacify it first, then extend Our majesty and kindness, and none will refuse to submit.'

sentences.zh: 」既而車駕南還雲中，懷服燕趙。

translations.literal: Thereafter the imperial carriage returned south to Yunzhong, and Yan and Zhao were won to submission.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage then returned south to Yunzhong, and Yan and Zhao submitted.

sentences.zh: 十數年間，諸種與庫莫奚亦皆滋盛。
