translations.literal: Within a dozen years the various tribes and the Kumo Xi alike all grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years the various tribes and the Kumo Xi all grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 及開遼海，置戍和龍，諸夷震懼，各獻方物。

translations.literal: When Liaohai was opened and garrisons were set at Helong, the various Yi were awed and each presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaohai was opened and garrisons placed at Helong, the frontier peoples were awed and each sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 高宗、顯祖世，庫莫奚歲致名馬文皮。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Gaozong and Emperor Xianzu, the Kumo Xi each year presented famed horses and patterned pelts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Gaozong and Xianzu, the Kumo Xi yearly sent famed horses and patterned furs.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign they sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，輒入塞內，辭以畏地豆于鈔掠，詔書切責之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe they repeatedly entered within the passes, pleading fear of Didouyu's raids; an imperial letter sharply rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe's fourth year they repeatedly entered the frontier passes, claiming fear of Didouyu raids; the court rebuked them sharply.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入寇安州，營燕幽三州兵數千人擊走之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they invaded Anzhou; several thousand soldiers from the garrisons of Yan and You drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year they invaded Anzhou and were driven off by several thousand troops from the Yan and You garrisons.

sentences.zh: 後復款附，每求入塞，與民交易。

translations.literal: Later they again submitted in good faith and repeatedly asked to enter the passes to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later they submitted again and repeatedly asked to enter the passes to trade with frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔曰：「庫莫奚去太和二十一年以前，與安營二州邊民參居，交易往來，並無疑貳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong issued an edict: 'Before the twenty-first year of Taihe, the Kumo Xi lived mingled with the frontier people of An and Ying and traded back and forth without suspicion.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong decreed: 'Before Taihe's twenty-first year, the Kumo Xi mingled with the people of An and Ying and traded without suspicion.'

sentences.zh: 至二十二年叛逆以來，遂爾遠竄。

translations.literal: Since their rebellion in the twenty-second year they have fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Since their rebellion in the twenty-second year they have fled far away.

sentences.zh: 今雖款附，猶在塞表，每請入塞與民交易。

translations.literal: Now, though they have submitted in good faith, they remain beyond the passes and repeatedly ask to enter and trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though they have now submitted, they remain beyond the passes and repeatedly ask to trade with our people.

sentences.zh: 若抑而不許，乖其歸向之心；

translations.literal: If We suppress and do not permit this, We thwart the heart of their turning toward Us.
translations.idiomatic: If We refuse, We thwart their desire to submit.

sentences.zh: 聽而不虞，或有萬一之警。

translations.literal: If We permit without precaution, there may be an emergency in one case out of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: If We permit without precaution, there may yet be trouble.

sentences.zh: 不容依先任其交易，事宜限節，交市之日，州遣上佐監之。

translations.literal: It is not fitting to allow trade as before without limit; the affair should be regulated, and on the day of the market the province shall send a senior aide to supervise.'
translations.idiomatic: They may no longer trade as freely as before; markets shall be regulated, and on trading days the province shall send an official to supervise.'

sentences.zh: 」自是已後，歲常朝獻，至於武定末不絕。

translations.literal: From this time onward they presented tribute every year down to the end of Wuding without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent annual tribute until the end of Wuding without interruption.

sentences.zh: 契丹國，在庫莫奚東，異種同類，俱竄於松漠之間。

translations.literal: The Khitan state lay east of the Kumo Xi; a different tribe of the same kind, they alike hid in the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan lay east of the Kumo Xi; a related but distinct people, they too hid in the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 登國中，國軍大破之，遂逃迸，與庫莫奚分背。

translations.literal: In the Dengguo era the state army routed them utterly; they fled in disorder and parted from the Kumo Xi.
translations.idiomatic: During Dengguo the imperial army routed them, and they fled apart from the Kumo Xi.

sentences.zh: 經數十年，稍滋蔓，有部落，於和龍之北數百里，多為寇盜。

translations.literal: After several decades they gradually spread and had tribes several hundred li north of Helong, and for the most part they raided and robbed.
translations.idiomatic: After several decades they spread until their tribes lay several hundred li north of Helong, mostly as raiders and robbers.

sentences.zh: 真君以來，求朝獻，歲貢名馬。

translations.literal: From the Zhenjun era onward they sought to come to court with tribute and each year presented famed horses.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenjun era they sought audience at court and yearly sent famed horses.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，使莫弗紇何辰奉獻，得班饗於諸國之末。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzu's time the envoy Mofohe Hechen came with tribute and was ranked to feast among the last of the states.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu the envoy Mofohe Hechen came with tribute and was seated at the feast among the lowest-ranked states.

sentences.zh: 歸而相謂，言國家之美，心皆忻慕，於是東北羣狄聞之，莫不思服。

translations.literal: Returning, they said to one another of the state's beauty; all their hearts rejoiced and admired, and when the tribes of the northeast Di heard of it, none did not think to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On returning they spoke of the empire's splendor with admiration, and when the northeastern tribes heard of it, all wished to submit.

sentences.zh: 悉萬丹部、何大何部、伏弗郁部、羽陵部、[6]日連部、匹絜部、黎部、[7]吐六于部等，[8]各以其名馬文皮入獻天府，遂求為常。

translations.literal: The Xiwandan, Hedahé, Fufuyu, Yuling, Rilian, Pijie, Li, and Tuliuyu divisions and others each presented their famed horses and patterned pelts to the imperial treasury and then asked that this become regular.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiwandan, Hedahé, Fufuyu, Yuling, Rilian, Pijie, Li, and Tuliuyu divisions and others each sent famed horses and patterned furs to the imperial treasury and asked to make the practice regular.

sentences.zh: 皆得交市於和龍、密雲之間，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: They all obtained to trade at markets between Helong and Miyun, and tribute did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: They all traded at markets between Helong and Miyun, and tribute flowed without cease.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，高句麗竊與蠕蠕謀，欲取地豆于以分之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, Goguryeo secretly plotted with the Rouran to take Didouyu and divide it.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe's third year Goguryeo secretly plotted with the Rouran to seize Didouyu and divide it.

sentences.zh: 契丹懼其侵軼，其莫弗賀勿于率其部落車三千乘、眾萬餘口，驅徙雜畜，求入內附，止於白狼水東。

translations.literal: The Khitan, fearing encroachment, their Mofohe Hewuyu led their tribes—three thousand carts and more than ten thousand mouths—driving mixed livestock, sought to enter and attach themselves within, stopping east of the White Wolf River.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing invasion, the Khitan chief Hewuyu led three thousand carts and more than ten thousand people with their herds to submit, settling east of the White Wolf River.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常朝貢。

translations.literal: From this time they presented tribute every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 後告饑，高祖矜之，聽其入關市糴。

translations.literal: Later they reported famine; Emperor Gaozu pitied them and allowed them to enter the passes to buy grain.
translations.idiomatic: When they later reported famine, Emperor Gaozu allowed them to enter the passes to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 及世宗、肅宗時，恒遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Suzong they constantly sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Shizong and Suzong they regularly sent envoys with local products.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，契丹使人祖真等三十人還，靈太后以其俗嫁娶之際，以青氊為上服，人給青氊兩匹，賞其誠款之心，餘依舊式。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, when the Khitan envoy Zuzhen and thirty others returned, Empress Dowager Ling, because at their weddings and betrothals blue felt was their upper garment, gave each person two bolts of blue felt to reward their sincere hearts; the rest followed the former pattern.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan envoy Zuzhen and thirty others returned in Xiping, Empress Dowager Ling gave each two bolts of blue felt—their ceremonial garment at weddings—to reward their sincerity.

sentences.zh: 朝貢至齊受禪常不絕。

translations.literal: Tribute missions continued without break down to the Qi acceptance of the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute continued without break down to the Qi dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 烏洛侯國，在地豆于之北，去代都四千五百餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Wuluohou lay north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wuluohou lay north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其土下濕，多霧氣而寒，民冬則穿地為室，夏則隨原阜畜牧。

translations.literal: Its soil was low and wet, with much fog and cold; in winter the people dug into the ground for dwellings, and in summer they followed the hills and marshes in herding.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low, wet, foggy, and cold; in winter they lived in pit-dwellings, in summer they pastured on the hills.

sentences.zh: 多豕，有穀麥。

translations.literal: They had many pigs and had grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They kept many pigs and grew grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 無大君長，部落莫弗皆世為之。

translations.literal: They had no great ruler; the tribal mofu were all hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: They had no great king; tribal chiefs held office by hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 其俗繩髮，皮服，以珠為飾。

translations.literal: Their custom was plaited hair, skins for dress, and pearls for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: They plaited their hair, wore skins, and adorned themselves with pearls.

sentences.zh: 民尚勇，不為姦竊，故慢藏野積而無寇盜。

translations.literal: The people valued courage and did not commit theft or robbery, and so grain was stored carelessly in the open without bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They were brave and honest; grain was left in the open without fear of thieves.

sentences.zh: 好獵射。

translations.literal: They loved hunting and archery.
translations.idiomatic: They loved hunting and archery.

sentences.zh: 樂有箜篌，木槽革面而施九弦。

translations.literal: In music they had the konghou, a wooden trough with a leather face and nine strings set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Their music included the konghou, a wooden trough with a leather face and nine strings.

sentences.zh: 其國西北有完水，東北流合于難水，其地小水皆注於難，東入于海。

translations.literal: Northwest of their state was the Wanshui, flowing northeast to join the Nanshui; the lesser waters of their land all poured into the Nan and entered the sea in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay the Wanshui, flowing northeast into the Nanshui; lesser streams all joined the Nan and reached the sea in the east.

sentences.zh: 又西北二十日行有于巳尼大水，所謂北海也。

translations.literal: Twenty days' travel northwest brought one to the great Yisini River, the so-called Northern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days northwest lay the great Yisini River, the so-called Northern Sea.

sentences.zh: 世祖真君四年來朝，稱其國西北有國家先帝舊墟，石室南北九十步，東西四十步，高七十尺，室有神靈，民多祈請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun they came to court, saying that northwest of their state was an old site of the state's Former Emperor—a stone chamber ninety paces north to south, forty east to west, and seventy feet high. The chamber had a numinous power and the people made many prayers there.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun's fourth year they came to court, reporting that northwest of their land stood a stone chamber of the Former Emperor's age—ninety paces by forty, seventy feet high—with a numinous presence to which the people prayed.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣中書侍郎李敞告祭焉，刊祝文於室之壁而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent Li Chang, Attendant of the Secretariat, to announce the sacrifice there, carved a prayer text on the chamber wall, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent Li Chang of the Secretariat to perform the sacrifice and carved a prayer on the chamber wall before returning.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夷狄之於中國，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: The historian says: The Yi and Di toward China are only tethered and bridled.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Toward China the Yi and Di are only tethered and bridled.

sentences.zh: 高麗歲修貢職，東藩之冠，榮哀之禮，致自天朝，亦為優矣。

translations.literal: Goguryeo yearly performed its tribute duties and was chief among the eastern frontier; the honors of mourning rites reaching it from the heavenly court were also exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo performed yearly tribute and stood first among the eastern frontier; the mourning honors sent from the court were exceptional as well.

sentences.zh: 其他碌碌，咸知款貢，豈牛馬內向，東風入律者也。

translations.literal: The others, commonplace, all knew to offer sincere tribute—was this cattle and horses turning inward, the eastern wind entering the pitch-pipes?
translations.idiomatic: The others, humbler still, all knew to offer tribute—was this the turning of cattle and horses inward, the eastern wind entering the pitch-pipes?

sentences.zh: 魏正始中入寇遼西安平 三國魏志卷三０東夷傳、隋書卷八一高麗傳「遼西安平」作「西安平」。

translations.literal: In the Wei Zhengshi era invasion of Liaoxi Anping: in the Biography of the Eastern Yi, juan 30 of the Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the Goguryeo Account, juan 81 of the Book of Sui, 'Liaoxi Anping' is written as 'Xi'anping.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhengshi-era invasion of Liaoxi Anping: the Records of the Three Kingdoms, Eastern Yi biography (juan 30), and the Book of Sui, Goguryeo account (juan 81), read 'Liaoxi Anping' as 'Xi'anping.'

sentences.zh: 按後漢書郡國志二安平國屬冀州，志五，西安平屬幽州遼東郡。

translations.literal: According to the Treatise on Commanderies and Kingdoms, juan 2 of the Book of the Later Han, Anping Kingdom belonged to Jizhou; according to juan 5, Xi'anping belonged to Liaodong Commandery in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of the Later Han, Treatise on Commanderies (juan 2), places Anping Kingdom in Jizhou; juan 5 places Xi'anping in Liaodong Commandery, Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼西郡沒有安平或西安平縣。

translations.literal: Liaoxi Commandery had neither Anping nor Xi'anping counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi Commandery had neither Anping nor Xi'anping county.

sentences.zh: 這裏「遼」字衍，或「遼」下脫「東」字。

translations.literal: Here the character 'Liao' is superfluous, or the character 'dong' is missing below 'Liao.'
translations.idiomatic: Here the character for 'Liao' is superfluous, or 'east' is missing after 'Liao.'

sentences.zh: 正始中世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗 諸本「宗」作「祖」，北史卷九四高麗傳作「宣武」。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era Emperor Shizong received the envoy Ruixifu at the Eastern Hall: in various editions 'Shizong' is written as 'Shizu'; the Goguryeo Account in Beishi, juan 94, has 'Xuanwu.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi-era audience with Ruixifu at the Eastern Hall: various editions read 'Shizong' as 'Shizu'; Beishi, Goguryeo account (juan 94), has 'Xuanwu.'

sentences.zh: 按上稱「正始」年號，自當作「世宗」，北史例稱帝號。

translations.literal: Considering that above the reign-period title 'Zhengshi' is named, it should read 'Shizong'; the Beishi regularly uses reign titles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign-period Zhengshi is named above, the text should read 'Shizong'; Beishi regularly uses reign titles.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 具弗伏國 按卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月兩見此部，都作「具伏弗」。

translations.literal: Jufufu state: according to the Basic Annals, juan 6, in the second month of the first year of Huangxing and the fourth month of the second year, this tribe appears twice, both written as 'Jufufu.'
translations.idiomatic: Jufufu state: the Basic Annals (juan 6) twice records this tribe in Huangxing 1.2 and 2.4 as 'Jufufu.'

sentences.zh: 下契丹傳有「伏弗郁部」，上脫「具」字，又「郁」「部」二字倒誤，但也可證這裏「弗伏」當作「伏弗」。

translations.literal: Below, in the Khitan Account, there is the 'Fufuyu Division'; above, the character 'ju' is missing, and the characters 'yu' and 'bu' are transposed in error, but this also proves that here 'fufu' should be 'fufu.'
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan account below has the 'Fufuyu Division'; 'ju' is missing above and 'yu' and 'bu' are transposed, confirming that 'fufu' here should be 'fufu.'

sentences.zh: 拔大何國 按下契丹傳有「何大何部」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「阿大何」。

translations.literal: Badahé state: according to the Khitan Account below there is the 'Hedahé Division'; the Basic Annals, juan 6, fourth month of the second year of Huangxing, has 'Adahé.'
translations.idiomatic: Badahé state: the Khitan account below has the 'Hedahé Division'; the Basic Annals (juan 6, Huangxing 2.4) has 'Adahé.'

sentences.zh: 這裏「拔」字當是「何」或「阿」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character 'ba' is probably a corruption of 'he' or 'a.'
translations.idiomatic: Here 'ba' is probably a corruption of 'he' or 'a.'

sentences.zh: 地豆于國 北史卷九四「于」作「干」。

translations.literal: Didouyu state: in Beishi, juan 94, 'yu' is written as 'gan.'
translations.idiomatic: Didouyu state: Beishi (juan 94) writes 'yu' as 'gan.'

sentences.zh: 按本書他處也多作「地豆于」，間亦作「干」，北史則多作「干」，間作「于」，今仍之。

translations.literal: According to other places in this book it is mostly written 'Didouyu,' sometimes 'Didougan'; Beishi mostly has 'gan,' sometimes 'yu'—the present text is retained.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere in this book the name appears mostly as Didouyu, sometimes Didougan; Beishi mostly uses gan. The present text is retained.

sentences.zh: 伏弗郁部羽陵部 按上勿吉傳見「具弗伏國」、「郁羽陵國」，卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月並見「具伏弗、郁羽陵」，這裏「伏弗」上當脫「具」字，「郁」「部」誤倒，當作「具伏弗部、郁羽陵部」。

translations.literal: Fufuyu Division, Yuling Division: according to the Wuji Account above there appear 'Jufufu state' and 'Yuyuling state'; the Basic Annals, juan 6, second month of the first year and fourth month of the second year of Huangxing, both have 'Jufufu, Yuyuling'—here above 'fufu' the character 'ju' is missing, and 'yu' and 'bu' are wrongly transposed; it should read 'Jufufu Division, Yuyuling Division.'
translations.idiomatic: Fufuyu and Yuling divisions: the Wuji account above has 'Jufufu state' and 'Yuyuling state'; the Basic Annals (juan 6, Huangxing 1.2 and 2.4) has 'Jufufu, Yuyuling.' 'Ju' is missing before 'fufu' and 'yu' and 'bu' are transposed; it should read 'Jufufu Division, Yuyuling Division.'

sentences.zh: 匹絜部黎部 按上勿吉傳及卷六顯祖紀皇興元年、二年並見「匹黎尒部」，通典卷二００契丹條作「匹黎部」。

translations.literal: Pijie Division, Li Division: according to the Wuji Account above and the Basic Annals, juan 6, first and second years of Huangxing, there appears the 'Pilier Division'; the Tongdian, juan 200, Khitan entry, has 'Pili Division.'
translations.idiomatic: Pijie and Li divisions: the Wuji account and Basic Annals (juan 6, Huangxing 1–2) have 'Pilier Division'; the Tongdian (juan 200, Khitan entry) has 'Pili Division.'

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「匹絜」下衍「部」字，本作「匹絜黎部」，誤分二部。

translations.literal: It is suspected that below 'Pijie' the character 'bu' is superfluous and the original read 'Pijieli Division,' wrongly divided into two divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Probably 'bu' after 'Pijie' is superfluous and the original was 'Pijieli Division,' wrongly split into two.

sentences.zh: 吐六于部 北史卷九四契丹傳「于」作「干」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「叱六手」，通典卷二００作「比六干」。

translations.literal: Tuliuyu Division: in Beishi, juan 94, Khitan Account, 'yu' is written as 'gan'; the Basic Annals, juan 6, fourth month of the second year of Huangxing, has 'Chiliushou'; the Tongdian, juan 200, has 'Biliugan.'
translations.idiomatic: Tuliuyu Division: Beishi, Khitan account (juan 94), writes 'yu' as 'gan'; the Basic Annals (juan 6, Huangxing 2.4) has 'Chiliushou'; the Tongdian (juan 200) has 'Biliugan.'

sentences.zh: 疑「吐」「比」皆「叱」字之訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected that both 'tu' and 'bi' are corruptions of the character 'chi.'
translations.idiomatic: Both 'tu' and 'bi' are probably corruptions of 'chi.'

sentences.zh: 「手」顯訛，「于」「干」不知孰是。

translations.literal: 'Shou' is clearly erroneous; whether 'yu' or 'gan' is correct is not known.
translations.idiomatic: 'Shou' is clearly wrong; whether 'yu' or 'gan' is correct remains uncertain.
